title: Second Half of the Chess Board
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI Capability Tracking
description: Interactive chessboard MicroSim illustrating exponential growth through the classic rice-on-the-chessboard story: one grain of rice on square 1, doubling on every square through square 64, with a slider that reveals squares one doubling step at a time.

learningObjectives: Explain why linear intuition fails to predict exponential (doubling) growth
Identify the point at which a doubling sequence becomes economically significant
Connect the second-half-of-the-chessboard metaphor to the trajectory of AI capability growth

keyQuestions: How many grains of rice are on square 32, and how does that compare to square 33?
Why does the same doubling rule feel harmless for the first half of the board but overwhelming in the second half?
What does this metaphor suggest about how organizations underestimate the pace of AI capability growth?
commonMisconceptions: Assuming a doubling process grows at a roughly constant, easy-to-plan-for rate
Believing that because early growth looks small, later growth will stay proportionally small
assessmentOpportunities: Ask learners to predict the grain count on square 40 before moving the slider there
Have learners explain in their own words why the second half of the board is where 'the real economic impact' occurs

dataSource.name: Wheat and chessboard problem (traditional)
dataSource.note: Grain counts are computed directly as powers of two (2^0 through 2^63); no external dataset is used.
